title: Crisp-Crusted French Baguettes
summary: An overnight starter builds flavour; the lean dough of flour, water, yeast and salt is folded rather than kneaded, shaped into three long loaves, proved in a floured cloth, slashed and baked very hot with steam.
equipment: baking stone or heavy upturned baking tray
razor blade or very sharp knife

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Starter
steps.text: Mix the starter and leave it overnight until bubbly.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine with the dough ingredients, rest, then work in the salt.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Give 4 sets of stretch-and-folds during a 2-hour rise.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Pre-shape, rest, then roll into 3 tapered baguettes and prove in the cloth.

steps.title: Score and bake
steps.text: Slash and bake on the hot stone with steam until crackling and 96 °C.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on a rack before cutting.

tips: Steam in the first minutes lets the loaves expand fully before the crust sets.
Hold the blade at a shallow angle and make quick, confident cuts.
A floured linen cloth pleated between the loaves keeps their shape as they prove.
storage: Baguettes are best on the day. Keep leftovers in a paper bag for up to 2 days and refresh in a hot oven, or freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
